title: Unit circle, radian measure, quadrants, and directed angles
section: Trigonometry ▷ Arbitrary Angles and Real Numbers
terms: unit circle; radian; degree measure; initial side; terminal side; positive angle; negative angle; quadrant; arc length.

exposition.text:
An angle in standard position begins on the positive x-axis; counterclockwise rotation is pos-

sin θ = y/r. The coordinate signs determine the signs of all six functions, while zero denom-
inators identify undefined values.
Radian measure is arc length divided by radius, θ = s/r, so π radians equals 180 degrees. On
the unit circle the terminal point is (cos θ, sin θ). Angles differing by 2πk have the same termi-
nal side. This definition treats sine and cosine as functions of arbitrary real numbers, including
negative numbers and numbers larger than one revolution.

question.text:
The terminal side of θ contains (−5, 12) and θ ∈ (π/2, π). What is sec θ + csc θ?
(A) −91/60 (B) 91/60 (C) −13/60 (D) −17/13 (E) 17/13

solution.text: Here r = 13, so sec θ = −13/5 and csc θ = 13/12. Their sum is (−156 + 65)/60 = −91/60.

question.text:
A wheel of radius 3 rotates clockwise through an arc length 17π. Starting at (3, 0) with center
at the origin, where does the marked point end?
√ √ √ √
(A) (3/2, 3 3/2) (B) (3/2, −3 3/2) (C) (−3/2, 3 3/2) (D) (−3/2, −3 3/2) (E) (0, 3)

solution.text:
The directed angle is −17π/3. Adding 6π gives the coterminal angle π/3, so the endpoint is

(3 cos(π/3), 3 sin(π/3)) = (3/2, 3 3/2).

For how many angles θ ∈ [0, 2π) does 2 cos θ + sin θ = 1 hold?
(A) 3 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 6 (E) 4

solution.text:
2
Writing s = sin θ gives 2s − s − 1 = 0, so s = 1 or s = −1/2. These yield one and two angles,
respectively.

question.text:
An angle θ has measure 90 + 180k degrees, where k is an integer. Which pair of functions is
undefined for every such θ?
(A) sin θ, cos θ (B) tan θ, sec θ (C) cot θ, csc θ (D) tan θ, csc θ (E) sec θ, cot θ

solution.text:
The radian measure is π/2 + kπ, whose terminal side lies on the y-axis. Thus cos θ = 0
and sin θ = ±1. Exactly tangent and secant divide by zero; cotangent is defined and equals
zero.

question.text:
